about: Oct 31 2026 audit fix: 13 Adobe facts checked by a fact checker; 59 canvas connections classified by four classifiers from Adobe pages; every classification re-checked by a skeptic (two for the first 45, two more for the 14 their input missed). A verdict with agree=false, or with corrected fields, carries the correction. Applied by audit_types.py.

facts.finding: Adobe sets two conditions for an impact report: the deployment must "Include at least 20 URLs from the High Potential URLs filter in a single deployment." and must be for a supported opportunity, given as examples: Recover Content Visibility, Add Table of Contents and Add LLM-friendly Summaries. Enrich Product Detail Pages is not named, and the PDP page never mentions the engine. Timing is a typical figure for one type only: "Recover Content Visibility experiments typically complete in about two weeks." A report is not guaranteed: outside the criteria the pages are still optimized but the report may not be generated, and even inside them "Impact Measurement Engine can only measure pages with sufficient data to produce reliable results", using a representative subset of the deployed URLs. The High Potential filter is optional for deploying but makes qualifying more likely. Adobe asks for no other content changes on those pages during measurement, keeps the measurement prompts out of the prompt quota, and for Trial customers recommends "the maximum 50 URLs" per deployment. For L03: its 'up to 10 URLs' basis cannot meet the 20-URL rule; agree one quantity of at least 20 eligible URLs, make the two-week report conditional on eligibility and enough data, and keep deployment and rollback acceptance separate from the measurement.
facts.quote: If these criteria aren't met, your pages will still be optimized but the corresponding Strategy with impact analysis may not be generated in Opportunity Workspace.
facts.title: Impact Measurement Engine | Adobe Brand Visibility (Experience League, last update October 30, 2026)

facts.finding: Two separate data paths, neither person-level. Into CJA: the Brand Visibility dataset holds only bot and AI agent requests read from CDN logs, aggregated and bucketed by URL and host, hour, bot type, CDN provider and status; "It does not contain any PII such as a user identifier, prompts, or responses." The dataset reference (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/analytics-platform/using/integrations/bv/reference, October 13, 2026) says "You cannot perform a person-level join from this dataset. The join operates at the URL and host level." and that the dataset holds no sessions or conversions. Human AI referrals: a person who clicks through from an AI answer is already in the customer's normal CJA web data; CJA does not label those visits, so someone builds a derived field on AI referring domains, and the Brand Visibility dataset is not needed for it. Bot demand and a page's conversions can be compared only at URL and host level, and "Whether the join succeeds depends on your own data collection." Out of CJA: Brand Visibility pulls aggregated CJA report data (page URL, referring domain, country, device, page views, visits, visitors, optional revenue and orders) into its Business Impact tab and "does not request ECID, IP address, cookie ID, or device ID through this integration." (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/resources/customer-journey-analytics-integration, August 11, 2026). Prerequisites: "You must have a Brand Visibility paid offering."; per the setup page (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/analytics-platform/using/integrations/bv/configure) "CDN access logs must be forwarded to and received by Adobe Brand Visibility for each Brand Visibility site before the Brand Visibility source connector can be viable."; the customer adds the dataset to a CJA connection and data view, because "Adobe does not modify your Customer Journey Analytics connections or data views."; and the Business Impact side must be enabled for the organization. Also, "some temporary processing of Brand Visibility data occurs in the United States". For the bv-cja connection: replace 'AI visibility tied to revenue' with AI agent activity by URL plus observed AI-referral visits and conversions, and show bot activity, monitored visibility, referral conversion and tested lift as separate measures.
facts.quote: Customer Journey Analytics does not label these visits as AI traffic on its own. To identify and group them, you create a derived field on the connection that matches the AI referring domains, then build segments and reports on that field. See Derived fields. You do not need the Brand Visibility dataset for this human traffic.
facts.title: Brand Visibility Integration | Adobe Customer Journey Analytics (Experience League, last update October 13, 2026)

facts.finding: Only one route is self-serve: AEM Cloud Service's managed Fastly, where an admin clicks Enable under Brands Management, CDN, and then "No further action is required on your end." (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/resources/optimize-at-edge/aemcs-managed-cdn, August 20, 2026). That route checks the detected CDN and fails with an error when the site is not on AEM Cloud Service Managed CDN (Fastly); it also needs the Adobe LLM Optimizer Users product profile (paid) or the LLMO Admin group (trial). A customer's own Fastly service follows the Fastly (BYOCDN) guide (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/resources/optimize-at-edge/fastly-byocdn, August 6, 2026): "Access to Fastly for your domain.", "An Edge Optimize API key retrieved from the Adobe Brand Visibility UI.", then "Add the following three VCL snippets to your Fastly service." (routing by AI user agent, cache-key separation, failover), optional WAF or Bot Manager allowlisting, and curl checks for bot and human traffic. The overview's CDN table lists AEM Cloud Service Managed CDN (Fastly) as the only Adobe Managed type; every other CDN, Fastly included, is Bring Your Own CDN, and "Routing must be configured at the outer CDN (the CDN closest to the client)." Commerce: none of the Brand Visibility pages checked (overview, both Fastly guides, log forwarding overview and Fastly guide, PDP enrichment, opportunities overview, quick start, what's new) mention Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure. Commerce's own docs say merchants "can create, modify, and deploy regular VCL snippets from the Admin or the Fastly API" (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-on-cloud/user-guide/cdn/custom-vcl-snippets/fastly-vcl-custom-snippets, August 20, 2025), so the BYOCDN snippets look possible there; that is an inference, not an Adobe statement. For C07: the exception for Commerce cloud stores on Fastly is not supported; scope it as CDN readiness and routing where required, verified per store (topology, outer CDN, owner, cache separation, rollback).
facts.quote: For AEM Cloud Service managed Fastly customers, the routing setup is self-serve and can be completed directly in the Adobe Brand Visibility UI. For customers using other CDN providers, your IT/CDN team needs to complete the required setup and prerequisites.
facts.title: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility (Experience League, last update August 26, 2026; C07's citation)

facts.finding: Adobe's sources conflict. The release notes (October 27, 2026) list the April 2026 Real-Time CDP integration as Limited Availability, on a page that says "All features are generally available unless indicated otherwise." The FAQ, updated the same day (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/brand-concierge-faq), says "In the current scope, Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge base (website and catalog), not from a live lookup of identity or journey state in Real-Time CDP." and calls profile and journey tailoring a future enhancement: "For now, the experience is consistent for anonymous visitors." The architecture blueprint the canvas cites for rtcdp-bc (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/blueprints-learn/architecture/use-case-patterns/conversational-experience-patterns/brand-concierge-conversational-experience, September 28, 2026) describes Real-Time CDP as a "Customer data platform providing real-time profile lookup for personalized conversations" with no availability label. The FAQ is also inconsistent inside itself: it says the assistant can "provide personalized responses informed by individual customer behavior", lists Experience Platform profiles as a data source, and lists handover to sales as roadmap while describing the Handoff to sales skill as available now. For rtcdp-bc and XA09: the baseline is the anonymous, public-information experience; profile context is Limited Availability and needs Adobe's written confirmation for the tenant, use case and region; the blueprint should not be the source for profile lookup.
facts.quote: Brand Concierge Integration with Real-Time CDP (Limited Availability): Enhance the quality and relevance of conversational responses by incorporating Real-Time CDP context, such as user attributes, behavioral signals, and prior interactions to better align replies with user intent.
facts.title: Current Release Notes | Adobe Brand Concierge (Experience League, last update October 27, 2026)

facts.finding: A short video page whose checklist is: "Confirm that knowledge sources are ingested, indexed, and free of broken or outdated pages."; test and approve tone, greeting and guardrail behavior; check the widget on desktop and mobile; "Score your golden evaluation set for correctness, helpfulness, and brand fit, including pricing and competitor questions."; verify script installation and analytics data flow; "Complete the dedicated checklists for meeting booking, live chat, and Marketo integration when enabled."; "Obtain stakeholder approval and confirm technical readiness with Adobe resources when they are involved."; and "Plan a gradual rollout, advancing only when results support the next stage." The rollout stages are examples, not a schedule. The FAQ adds that "many implementations reach go-live in about 6-9 weeks".
